items.stem: What is the main purpose of applying cut-off at month-end?

options.text: To record transactions in the correct accounting period
options.rationale: Correct: cut-off ensures revenues and expenses fall in the period they relate to.

options.text: To delete last month's journal entries
options.rationale: Cut-off does not delete prior entries.

options.text: To close user access to the accounting system
options.rationale: Cut-off is about period allocation, not system access.

options.text: To calculate the tax charge for the year
options.rationale: Tax computation is a separate exercise.

items.explanation: Correct: cut-off ensures revenues and expenses fall in the period they relate to.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about balance-sheet reconciliations are correct?

options.text: A reconciliation should explain and support the balance, not just show it matches
options.rationale: Correct: a quality reconciliation substantiates the balance with evidence.

options.text: Reconciling items should be identified, aged and cleared over time
options.rationale: Correct: open items must be tracked and resolved, not left indefinitely.

options.text: A matching total alone proves the account is correct
options.rationale: Balances can match while containing offsetting unexplained items.

options.text: Reconciliations remove the need for any supporting documents
options.rationale: Supporting evidence is central to a reconciliation.

options.text: Only the cash account ever needs reconciling
options.rationale: Many control and subledger accounts require reconciliation.

items.explanation: Correct: a quality reconciliation substantiates the balance with evidence.

items.stem: Why must an accrual usually be reversed in the following period?

options.text: To avoid double-counting the cost when the actual invoice is later recorded
options.rationale: Correct: reversing clears the estimate so the real invoice is not counted twice.

options.text: Because accruals are not allowed under accrual accounting
options.rationale: Accruals are a core part of accrual accounting.

options.text: To increase the current month's profit
options.rationale: Reversal is about accuracy, not inflating profit.

options.text: Because reversals delete the original entry's audit trail
options.rationale: A reversal is itself recorded, preserving the audit trail.

items.explanation: Correct: reversing clears the estimate so the real invoice is not counted twice.
